description: Experience the iconic flavors of Butter Chicken, a rich and creamy Indian curry featuring tender chicken simmered in a spiced tomato and butter sauce. This classic Murgh Makhani recipe delivers a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy notes, perfect for a comforting meal. Its velvety texture and aromatic spices make it a beloved dish worldwide.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and salt. Mix well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tbsp butter in a large pan or pot over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 7-10 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter. Add the chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor
instructions.text: Stir in the remaining 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, then add the tomato puree and soaked cashews. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water if it is too thick. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth sauce. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, and sugar (if using). Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Stir in the heavy cream just before serving and heat gently without boiling.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For extra tender chicken, marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator.
Do not skip the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves); it adds an authentic, slightly bitter and aromatic depth to the Butter Chicken.
For a restaurant-style silky smooth sauce, ensure you blend the sauce ingredients thoroughly and strain it through a fine-mesh sieve.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a culinary hug, a vibrant symphony of flavors that has captivated palates worldwide. Originating from the bustling kitchens of Delhi, this iconic Indian chicken recipe has transcended borders to become a global favorite. Its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of marinated chicken, creates an unforgettable experience that is both comforting and exquisitely indulgent. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality flavor in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. This article will guide you through the classic preparation of Murgh Makhani, ensuring you master this beloved Indian delicacy.

## What is Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its genesis is often attributed to Kundan Lal Gujral, founder of Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, shortly after the partition of India in 1947. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken pieces were simmered in a rich tomato gravy enhanced with butter and cream, creating a dish that quickly became a sensation.

At its heart, Murgh Makhani is characterized by succulent pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoori-cooked or grilled) bathed in a velvety smooth, mildly spiced tomato sauce. The sauce's signature sweetness comes from tomatoes and sometimes a touch of honey or sugar, balanced by the tang of yogurt or cream, and aromatic spices like garam masala, fenugreek (kasuri methi), and cardamom. The generous use of butter and cream gives it its luxurious texture and name. While often compared to Chicken Tikka Masala, Butter Chicken typically has a milder, sweeter profile and a smoother, richer gravy, making it incredibly appealing to a wide audience, including those new to Indian cuisine. It’s the ultimate comfort food, deeply satisfying and utterly delicious.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key ingredients for both the chicken marinade and the exquisite sauce.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt (full-fat for best results)
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or paprika)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp cumin powder
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tbsp lemon juice

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water (for blending cashews)
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
*   1/4 cup heavy cream
*   1 tbsp honey or sugar (optional, to balance tartness)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making classic Butter Chicken is a labor of love, but the steps are straightforward and rewarding.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) or a grill pan/skillet over medium-high heat. If using an oven, arrange marinated chicken on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes until cooked through and slightly charred. If using a skillet, add a little oil and cook chicken in batches until browned and cooked through. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil over medium heat. Add chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in crushed tomatoes (or puree), red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and flavors to meld.

5.  **Add Cashews and Simmer:** While the tomatoes are cooking, blend the soaked cashews with 1/2 cup water until completely smooth. Add this cashew paste to the tomato mixture. Stir well, then add garam masala. Continue to simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.

6.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the entire sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.

7.  **Finish the Sauce:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp butter, heavy cream, and crushed kasuri methi. If using, add honey or sugar to taste. Adjust salt if necessary.

8.  **Combine Chicken and Sauce:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Gently stir to coat the chicken completely. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Do not boil vigorously once cream is added.

9.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving truly exceptional Butter Chicken comes down to a few key techniques and considerations.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken:** The authentic smoky flavor of Murgh Makhani comes from tandoor-cooked chicken. If you don't have a tandoor, pan-frying or grilling the chicken until it gets some nice char marks will add a similar depth of flavor. A small piece of charcoal smoked in a bowl of hot oil and placed in the pot with the finished dish (a technique called *dhungar*) can also impart a smoky aroma.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality, ripe tomatoes or canned crushed tomatoes. They form the backbone of the sauce, so their flavor is crucial.
*   **Smooth Sauce:** Blend the sauce thoroughly until it's absolutely silky smooth. Any graininess will detract from the luxurious mouthfeel. Passing it through a sieve after blending is a chef's secret for perfection.
*   **Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** This spice is non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken. Crush it between your palms before adding to release its aromatic oils. It adds a unique, slightly bitter, savory note that defines the dish.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust! The beauty of Murgh Makhani is its balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Add a little more honey/sugar if it's too tart, or a pinch more salt.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a star that shines brightest with the right supporting cast. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy naan (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is the ultimate companion, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a light, fluffy counterpoint to the creamy curry.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based side dish, such as cucumber raita, offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Salad:** A simple onion and cucumber salad with a lemon dressing can add a fresh crunch.
*   **Pickles:** Indian mango pickle or lime pickle can add an extra layer of tangy, spicy flavor for those who enjoy it.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is divine, it's also wonderfully adaptable.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas for a delicious vegetarian version. Follow the same marination and cooking steps for paneer/tofu, adjusting cooking times.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** For a dairy-free alternative, use coconut yogurt for marination, coconut oil instead of butter, and full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use light cream. You can also grill the chicken without oil.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper. For less, stick to Kashmiri chili powder or paprika.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have nut allergies, you can omit the cashews. The sauce will be slightly less thick, but still delicious. Alternatively, use melon seeds (magaz) or sunflower seeds, soaked and blended, for a similar thickening effect.

Embracing the art of making Butter Chicken at home is a journey into the heart of Indian cuisine. With these detailed instructions and tips, you're well on your way to creating a truly memorable Murgh Makhani that will impress family and friends. So gather your ingredients, put on some good music, and get ready to savor the unparalleled delight of homemade Butter Chicken!
